_comment: Edit freely. Title keywords are case-insensitive whole-word matches; end one with * to match word prefixes (pentest* matches pentester, pentesting). Exclude wins over include.
_languages_comment: Working languages you have. An ad that requires any other language (German, French, Dutch, ...), or is written in one, is flagged in the JD packet and scored as a language blocker (skip).
_max_age_comment: Drop roles posted more than this many days ago (0 = no limit). Roles with no posted date are kept.
_employment_comment: Permanent roles only: a match in the title or in the employment type the ATS reports drops the role. "Smart contract" is exempt.

tiering._comment: Score = best title keyword + seniority words + country + bonuses. score >= tier1_min_score is Tier 1. Keywords use the same whole-word/* rules as title_include.

sponsorship._comment: Fuzzy name-match thresholds (0-100) against the UK/NL sponsor registers. >= fuzzy_yes is yes; between the two is unknown.

board._comment: New roles become issues labelled 'role'; the GitHub Project auto-adds them. baseline_tiers applies to the very first run only.

scoring._comment: Roles Claude scores automatically at the start of each session (freshest unscored Tier 1 first), before answering. 0 = only when asked. Each role costs 0.25-0.5% of a session (measured on Pro).
scoring._linkedin_job_pages_comment: true: when scoring a role whose ad is on LinkedIn, Claude in Chrome may read that one job page in your logged-in browser to get the description (one page at a time, read-only). LinkedIn's terms ban automated access; this is your risk to accept. false: Claude asks you to paste the description.

linkedin_posts._comment: true: at the start of a session Claude in Chrome may read LinkedIn post-search results (hiring posts by recruiters and hiring managers, and the people who repost them) in your logged-in browser, to find roles the job boards miss. Read-only, never reacts, comments, connects or messages. LinkedIn's terms ban automated access; this is your risk to accept. false: nothing runs.

referrals._comment: Days to wait for a reply to a referral ask before the session brief suggests a follow-up or applying directly.
referrals._linkedin_comment: true: when you are about to apply to one role and ask, Claude in Chrome may read LinkedIn people-search results in your logged-in browser to find a recruiter or hiring manager. Read-only, never connects or messages. LinkedIn's terms ban automated access; this is your risk to accept. false: Claude gives you search links to open yourself.
